The 220 yds heats went off uneventfully with Brian Morris and Charlie Jones qualifying easily for the final. The next event concerning the Bels was the 440 yds which was run as a straight final, and taking part was our 4 x 440 relay team.

Brian Morris and John Davies have already recorded good times for the 440 yds. and 1500 metres respectively, whilst Alan Black and Malcolm Robinson look set for their best seasons yet.

Belgravians did quite well at this meeting with Dave Ansell beating 22 ft. in his first long jump of the season and Charlie Jones lowering his previous best quarter time by 0.9s., also in his first attempt this season. Our International quarter-miler, Brian Morris ran 150 yards in the good time of 15.0s.

Our 4 x 110 yds. team failed to materialize and in the 4 x 440 yds. we were fifth. Frank Wright, Pat Fox, Alan Jackson and Brian Morris constituted our team. The medley relay saw us finish in 6th place.

Brian Morris and John Davies showed their class by cantering home in the 440 and 880 respectively and virtually clinched the match for us. An excellent start to the season was made by Norman Caves in the triple jump with 45'4", only 13" less than his highly ranked best of last year.

Our own John Davies, Brian Morris, Clive Ryan, Frank Wright and D. McCorquindale were competing elsewhere, and with Stan Vickers Eric Hall, Norman Caves, Mal Ash and Andorka also unavailable our team could not be said to be truly representative of the name of Belgrave.

Brian Morris won the senior 'A' 220 in 23.8 whilst Alan Jackson secured second place in the 'B' with 23.6 - a grand start to the meeting. Dave Mitchell won a well judged quarter in the good time of 52.1 and Alan Black obtained further points by finishing 4th in the 880.
Brian Morris ran one of his best races of the season to record 48.4 secs to finish 3rd, behind Ted Sampson and Chris Lindsey who both clocked 47.7 secs.
Ron Holtum was first past the post in the 220 yds, with 22.8 whilst Brian Morris reversed the "Southern" result by winning the quarter in 49.3 from Ted Sampson of Blackheath.

In the National Police Championships, held at Belle Vue Manchester on July 22nd, Brian Morris scored a notable double, winning the 220 in 22.4 and the 440 in 48.8.
The highlight of this season, so far, is undoubtedly the struggle for supremacy between Peter Eldridge and Brian Morris, in the quarter-mile.
Brian Morris finished first in the final of the 220 yards with 22.6 seconds, and later came out to make it a double by retaining his 440 yards title with a winning time of 49.4 seconds.
